utterances.text: Mr. Stojic, I have now a series of documents in front of me. They are excerpts from the court file against Danilusko Kajtez. All these documents have been disclosed. And now I want to go one by one and just -- I want you to make comments. The first document is a document which has already been prenumbered -- exhibited, sorry. P781.1.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: I must apologise. I must apologise. It's document 812. I'm sorry. I think you all have this document in front of you, so we don't need to put it on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: This document was issued at the health centre Sanski Most and it is a report on an investigation in the village of Kruhari. You can see the list of the names. Do you know the people who are listed in this report?

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Are those people who were killed on the 2nd of November in --

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: -- the Glamosnica forest? And is it correct to say that five of them were killed together with you and the remaining four were killed during that fire you heard from the distance and you learned about that incident in the hospital in Banja Luka? Is it correct?

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: The other document which I want to show to the witness is document 813, P813. This is an indictment issued by the military prosecutor's office in Banja Luka, and it is an indictment against Danilusko Kajtez and Milos Maksimovic. Mr. Stojic, can you just read the paragraph below which starts on 2nd November, 1992.

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC
utterances.text: I can.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Oh, have you -- I'm sorry. I'm sorry. Have you read this passage before?

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC
utterances.text: No, I haven't. It's the first time I've seen it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: So can you please slowly read it.

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC
utterances.text: "On the 2nd November 1992, in the village of Glamosnica, Sanski Most municipality, the aforementioned using the automatic weapons they had, waylaid male inhabitants of the village of Skrljevita, interrogated them on the pretext of finding out who had weapons and how well they were organised. They then executed Ivo Tutic, son of Ante" -- but this Ivo, his father is Nikola -- "from Skrljevita; Bono Tutic, son of Marijan from Skrljevita." It's not Talic but Ptalec. "Tomica, son of Josip." He's from Croatia but he's from Skrljevita. "Josip Banovic, son of Ivo from Skrljevita; Zare Nikic, son of Martin, from Skrljevita; Pero Nikic, son of Marko, from Skrljevita; Ante Tutic, son of Ivo from Skrljevita; Drago Tadic, son of Nikola from Skrljevita; and Karlo Tadic, son of Marko from Skrljevita."

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Thank you. Is this an accurate description of the event which occurred on the 2nd November 1992?

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC
utterances.text: The description is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Now I want to proceed. And I want to show the witness the other document which was pre-numbered P814.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: There are two copies of the same document. One is illegible. And the other is a better copy.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Do you know, Mr. Stojic, whether anybody was -- Danilusko Kajtez was arrested for this event?

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC
utterances.text: That's what I heard. I heard that he was arrested.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: So this document statement on 7th of December 1992, Danilusko Kajtez was taken into custody. Did you hear that he was released from the custody?

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC
utterances.text: I heard that too.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Can I show the witness another document, which was pre-numbered P815. And there are also two copies of the B/C/S version because one is illegible.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And it says that Danilusko Kajtez was released from the custody. Can you see the date of ...?

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can. The 2nd of January, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: So he didn't stay more than one month in the custody.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Then we have another document. And I think you can stay there. It's a document pre-numbered 816, when Danilusko Kajtez was again taken into custody.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Have you seen this document before?

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC
utterances.text: No. It's the first time I see this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And then we have another document pre-numbered P817, which shows that Danilusko Kajtez was released from the custody on 14 of March, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Do you know what happened to Danilusko Kajtez after he was released from the custody?

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC
utterances.text: I know that he was in Sanski Most; I heard that. I heard that he obtained a cafe in Sanski Most as a prize. It was called Ruski Czar or the "Russian Tsar." The owner was a Muslim. He was in Sanski Most from the centre towards the Catholic church, on the road Banja Luka-Sanski Most, through the Sasina village. I heard that he did that and that he responded to the name "Dane, the Chetnik."

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Mr. Stojic, now I want to show you another document which was pre-numbered P818. And it is a decision where it was approved -- approving -- a decision approving the change of personal name from Danilusko Kajtez, and he will legally use the name Nikola Kovacevic. Did you hear that Danilusko Kajtez would change his name?

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC
utterances.text: Yes, I heard it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: I have two more documents. The first one was pre-numbered 81 -- P819. And it is a decision that on 7 of December 2000 Danilusko Kajtez, who is still named here as Danilusko Kajtez shall be remanded into custody. And then I want to show you another document which was pre-numbered 820, which is from 17 of January 2002. And it is a ruling that Danilusko Kajtez, again called with this name -- that Danilusko Kajtez is to be tried in absentia. It means that until January 2002 no action was done. Have you ever been called to -- as a witness in this procedure which took place in front -- in Banja Luka district court?

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC
utterances.text: I wasn't called ever.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Were you interviewed while you were in hospital in -- I apologise -- in connection with this incident?

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC
utterances.text: Yes. In hospital an inspector from Sanski Most came. But before I was in the cell he introduced himself as being Mile Dosen.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: So after this interview, you weren't called as a witness in the procedure of -- in Banja Luka; is it correct?

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC
utterances.text: I was not. That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: I want to remind that already exhibited was a document P781.2, which is a letter of Danilusko Kajtez to Vlado Vrkes threatening if he didn't help to get him to release. Your Honour, I've concluded my examination-in-chief of Grgo Stojic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Could I just ask you one question, sir. Have you ever heard of the name of Goran Vukojevic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I have heard it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And Todo Vokic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Did they have any connection with the events that took place on the 2nd November, 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Those are the two men who were there when we were approaching the other four, when the execution was carried out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So if one states that they could have been witnesses in the case against Dane Kajtez, that would be a correct statement.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And I notice that in this document, your name is not mentioned anywhere. Can you give us a reason for that? You are not indicated as a possible witness or a probable witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Can you think of a reason?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's not clear to me at all why I'm not mentioned as a surviving witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Probably because in this way they can be free.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Who is going to go first? Yes. You are now going to be cross-examined by Madam Fauveau, who is counsel for General Talic. Madam Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Stojic, before beginning I should like to express my deep sympathy for the tragedy that you lived through on that day in November 1992. I am going to first ask you a few questions about that event, or more precisely the circumstances under which this murder took place. And then I will have a few more general questions for you. At the time of this murder on the 2nd of November, 1992 there were no military operations in Skrljevita; is that right?

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: And at the time of the murder, there were no tanks or military vehicles close to the scene of the crime.

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC
utterances.text: They were not seen there.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: You said in your written statement, and you also said today, that Kajtez was wearing civilian clothes; is that right?

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: And you also spoke of Goran Vukojevic, who was in uniform and who wore a military belt; is that right? A belt of the military police; is that right?

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC
utterances.text: Not just any uniform. A camouflage uniform. And a belt worn by the military police, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: And you said that he had a beret with a cockade and the Serb cross and the four S's; is that right?

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. The four S's were on the barrel -- on the rifle butt, on the butt of his light machine-gun.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Is it not true that regularly -- regular military police did not wear berets with cockades and the Serb cross?

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC
utterances.text: They told us that they were Seselj's army, just before killing us.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Seselj's army would be a paramilitary unit, would it not?

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC
utterances.text: Yes, they were part of the paramilitary formation then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, Ms. Korner, because I have a suspicion. I want to make sure that the witness knows what "paramilitary" means. What do you understand by "paramilitary"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The paramilitary, in my opinion, is the unit outside control -- the control of the military command and the civilian command.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You may go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I don't think -- I don't think it matters much. And as much as I would like to get into defence mode, Your Honour referred to Madam Fauveau as Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Oh, I'm sorry. I'm sorry. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I suppose one of us should be insulted. I'm not sure who.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I certainly am not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Fauveau. Please.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: You described today how after these murders that took place you went to your village of Skrljevita and how once there the neighbours helped you.

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Is it not true that a woman called Nada, who was a Serb, also helped you?

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC
utterances.text: Yes. But she comes from a mixed marriage. That is true too, yes. Her name is Nada Ilicic. She worked in my village. She lived at my place, and she knows everyone in Skrljevita.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: That woman, Nada Ilicic, did she accompany you to Sanski Most?

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC
utterances.text: She called the ambulance once we reached her.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: And did the ambulance come?

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC
utterances.text: No. We went in a horse-drawn cart.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: As far as Sanski Most -- going to Sanski Most, did you have to pass through any checkpoints?

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC
utterances.text: Yes. At the very entrance to Sanski Most, that is, the town itself. Close to the Catholic church.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: You passed through there without any problems.

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC
utterances.text: Yes, on that occasion we passed through without any problems.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: When you arrived at the Sanski Most hospital, were you interrogated by the police?

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC
utterances.text: I was.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: And these police officers, were they polite with you?

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC
utterances.text: Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: And you told them exactly what happened?

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC
utterances.text: What I told you here I told them.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: And afterwards at the Banja Luka hospital, this other inspector, Mile Dosen, that you mentioned today, he also arrived, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: And you told him too exactly what happened.

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did. That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the registrar give the witness Exhibit P813.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, a moment ago you saw this indictment, and you said that the description of the crime is quite correct; is that right?

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Is your copy as -- if your copy is as bad as mine, I don't think you can see the date. But apparently the date appears on the English version as being the 2nd of June, 1993.

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: So an indictment was issued after you told these inspectors what had happened.

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: And in 1993 -- the summer of 1993, you were already in Croatia.

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Is it not true that you were not called as a witness because you were in Croatia?

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC
utterances.text: I don't know that. But I never received any documents in Sanski Most. And how could I get them, when the village was already empty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Madam Fauveau, if you look at the second page of that document, the penultimate paragraph, it says: "The Prosecution's proposal to hear the testimony of witnesses Goran Vukojevic and Todo Vokic because they are the only surviving witnesses, the only surviving witnesses." That's what it states here.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The only killers.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. But there were no relations between Croatia and Republika Srpska at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, can you confirm that there were no relations as far as you know at the time between Croatia and Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC
utterances.text: Then how could these people have been expelled from Bosnia-Herzegovina and how could they cross into Croatia?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether there were any diplomatic relations or any other relations between Croatia and Republika Srpska or whether the postal services functioned between Republika Srpska and Croatia?

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC
utterances.text: The postal services did not function, but there were humanitarian organisations that were functioning.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: When you came to Croatia, did you send your address to Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC
utterances.text: To whom would I do that?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please look at Exhibit 816, please. Is it a decision dated the 9th of July, 1993 according to which Danilusko Kajtez was placed in detention, pre-trial detention?

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please look at Exhibit 817 now, please. It is the ruling according to which Danilusko Kajtez was temporarily released on the 14th of March, 1995?

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: And if you look at the first paragraph, below the word "statement of reasons," the decision refers to a decision dated the 9th of July, 1993 on pre-trial detention; is that right?

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: So it is -- is it correct to say that according to these two decisions, Danilusko Kajtez was in detention since July 1993 up to March 1995? From July until March.

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC
utterances.text: That is not correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: How do you know it is not true?

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC
utterances.text: Because the Serbs who lived there know that.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you explain in that case the decision of March 1995.

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC
utterances.text: March 1995? As far as I know Sanski Most was liberated on the 20th of October, 1995. And as far as I know, he was in detention at the beginning of 1993 and he was held at the Manjaca camp, where they had a detention centre. That is the information that reached me. How then could he have had that cafe that I already mentioned called "the Russian Tsar," that used to be owned by a Muslim, when Nada's daughter knew him personally and she went to that cafe that he ran.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, did you personally see Danilusko Kajtez between 1993 and 1995 anywhere?

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC
utterances.text: How could I see him? I was in Croatia and he was in Sanski Most.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Would you allow for the possibility, then, that he was indeed in detention between July 1993 and March 1995?

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC
utterances.text: You can put anything on paper. Paper stands for anything. Paper will tolerate anything.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: I go back for a moment to your detention at the Banja Luka hospital. You said that a given moment you were placed in a cell.

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: This room, it was in the hospital, was it not?

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the registrar give the witness DT16 and DT17, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: DT16 is a letter from the bishop of Banja Luka to the Zagreb hospital; is that right?

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC
utterances.text: It was not addressed. It was given to me to carry with me. It's a recommendation for doctor's treatment.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters would kindly request that it be placed on the ELMO if possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Usher, please place it on the ELMO and try to move the ELMO as near to the witness as possible so that he can refer to it. It's needed to be on the ELMO by the interpreters. If you have the English version, you can put the English version on the ELMO, and he will have --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: -- the one in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: So this letter was written by Bishop Franjo Komarica and then given to you; is that right?

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Before you gave this letter to the hospital, did anyone else have occasion to see it? Was anyone else able to see it?

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC
utterances.text: No, no one could see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: So in this letter, Bishop Komarica writes that you were released from the Banja Luka hospital on the 11th of December. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC
utterances.text: I've already said that.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: This letter makes absolutely no mention of the prison. It only mentions the hospital.

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you. How could the letter mention a prison when we know where Bishop Komarica was in 1992? Was he in Banja Luka? And it was not the bishop who was in prison. I was in prison.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: You said that between the moment you received this letter and the moment the letter was given to the Zagreb hospital, no one was able to see that letter. Why then wouldn't the bishop have written the truth?

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC
utterances.text: I don't know that. I show you what the International Red Cross said where I was. Here is the document.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: I can't see it from here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Can you put it on the ELMO for the time being, please. In what language is it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's in the Croatian language.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. I'm going to -- exactly. I'm going to do that. But first I want to see it. Yes. Now --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And there's this certificate too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: There are two ways we can go about this. The witness can be handed this document and I can ask him to read out its contents. And obviously we'll have it photocopied and distributed. That's one way of dealing with it. That's another one?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I've got this document here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Is there an agreement that we should photocopy everything to start with? Is that in English?

utterances.speaker: MR. USHER
utterances.text: B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But that's not the same document. No? Is it the same --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. This is a certificate --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's start with the first of the documents that you put -- that were put on the ELMO. Let's start with that one. Usher, please give it to the witness. Take that document in your hand, sir, and tell us what it says, what's written there.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This was a message sent to me by my brothers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Slowly. Read out slowly, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "Croatian Red Cross, 109, at the International Committee of the Red Cross, the 25th of February, received." Ante and Ivo Stojic sent it to me. That's right. From Zagreb. "Recipient, Grgo Stojic. Date of birth, 1968. Sex, male. Address, Banja Luka hospital." And at the bottom it says, beneath in red: "11th of December, Tunjice - released." It's an abbreviation for "released." "According to the information that the International Red Cross has -- that the International Committee of the Red Cross in Banja Luka has, the above-mentioned person was released on the 11th of December, 1992 from the Tunjice prison. And the International Committee of the Red Cross in Banja Luka on the 11th of February 1993. Signature."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Now, we can have someone go and photocopy that document straight away, please. And you have a second document that you want to show us?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I have. A certificate from the International Committee of the Red Cross, from Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Could you read it out to us, please, slowly.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can. "Zagreb, the 27th of January, 1993. Certificate. "We hereby confirm that Grgo Stojic, son of Dragan, born on the 30th of January, 1968 in Sanski Most, who was registered by delegates of the International Committee of the Red Cross on the 19th of November, [Realtime transcript read in error "1993"] 1992 in the Banja Luka prison. He has been visited regularly from the 19th of November, 1992 up until the 3rd of December, 1992. He was released on the 11th of December, 1992." And here it says "according to what the authorities have stated." There's a signature, "the delegate of the service for searches."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, there's a mistake in the transcript. What he read was -- where it says: "We hereby confirm," where he's quoting. It says that he was "Registered by the International Committee of the Red Cross on 19 November 1993." What he said was 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You've heard what Mr. Ackerman has said. Is he -- is what Mr. Ackerman has just stated correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's correct to say that I was registered on the 19th of November, 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ackerman. Madam Fauveau, do you want these two documents tendered as evidence for your client?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So those will be DT18 and 19.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. We will give you the originals back. Yes, Madam Fauveau, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: These two documents date back to 1993; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: They were written after you had arrived in Croatia; isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: And they were written in Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC
utterances.text: One document was written in Banja Luka -- or rather, it was certified there.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't comment on this before seeing the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It will soon be available, Madam Fauveau, give or take two minutes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: In the meantime, could you have a look at document DT17. Is that a document from Caritas in Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Which was addressed to the prison exchange commission of the Croatian community of Herceg-Bosna?

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: And this document refers to a list of prisoners.

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: The persons who were detained in the camps in prisons and in hospitals in Banja Luka -- and in the surroundings of Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: And then this document mentions your name.

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: And further on, the document states that you were in the hospital in Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC
utterances.text: In the cell in the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: This document doesn't mention a prison.

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC
utterances.text: Well, you should have been there in 1992 to see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Nevertheless this document does mention that people were detained in camps, prisons, and hospitals. But as far as you were concerned, it says that you were in the hospital.

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC
utterances.text: Yes, but in prison.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: According to this document, were you in prison?

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC
utterances.text: On the basis of this document -- well, you can see all three men were in hospital in Banja Luka and their lives were endangered, because the witnesses were inconvenient -- "Are inconvenient witnesses to crimes in the municipality of Sanski Most. The above-named people are from Skrljevita, municipality of Sanski Most." And the signature says -- if that's a hospital in normal conditions, as it should be, according to the conventions of the International Committee of the Red Cross, then I -- in such a case, our lives would not have been in danger.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: I’m not arguing the conditions that may have prevailed in that hospital, but my only question was were you in the hospital itself and not in a prison of Tunjice, at least on the basis of this document?

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC
utterances.text: I was in the urology ward in the hospital, in cell number 9. First of all, I was in cell number 8.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah. You explained that. You don't need to go through it again.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I have several general questions. Would it be better to stop now and continue tomorrow? I will need 15 minutes tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. And -- so Madam Fauveau will need 15 minutes. May I ask you, Mr. Ackerman -- yes, Mr. Trbojevic, how long do you think your cross-examination will last?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I was intending to cross-examine for 15 minutes. If Ms. Fauveau doesn't put the questions that I intend to put. It can only be less than that, less than 15 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I know where you stand. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can I just tell Your Honours that for the next witness, there's no List of Documents because all I'm going to do is use the ones that are attached to his statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Okay. I thank you. Sir, we need to stop here because this is the agreed time for adjourning. We will resume tomorrow at 2.15 in the afternoon. Hopefully we will not need to keep you waiting like we did today. And I'm sure that tomorrow we will finish with your evidence so that you will be in a position to return home. I thank you, and we'll see you again tomorrow. Thank you, everyone. And tomorrow afternoon we will be meeting in this same courtroom, Courtroom I. Okay? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
